title: I’m trying to pass a prop firm with algo trading with Claude code and I need help please
author: Ai_copywriting_agent
selftext: I’m trying to take advantage of the convex payout structure I’ve tried Orderflow , vwap fades , mean reversions and I’m now on ict I have an indicator on TradingView that has worked in the last week and would’ve of passed but these are its backtest results I can’t get anything better than these , I think I need a high wr 1:1rr could someone please share wisdom or code 🙏

comments.author: Tripple_sneeed
comments.body: I would recommend trying something that doesn’t blow up your account with an 80% drawdown

replies.author: Ai_copywriting_agent
replies.body: Yes but how ? I think the lowest ive got was 23%

replies.author: Tripple_sneeed
replies.body: In this situation, it seems to be a fundamentally bad strategy combined with way too much leverage

replies.author: Ai_copywriting_agent
replies.body: I’ve been aiming for 1:1 rr with high win rate but just cannot seem to find it

replies.author: Tripple_sneeed
replies.body:
Did you think it would be easy? Jesus dude. If you had nailed a +80% agr backtest on the first, tenth, or even 100th prompt to claude it would just mean that your backtester is leaking future data somewhere. Been there. 

  
What you're trying to do can be done, but no part of it will come easily, with or without an LLM.

replies.author: BarLeDuc9000
replies.body: Agree it simply is not easy. And Claude will give you the impression you can make it. You will be able to develop strategies fast backtest forward test robustness test and all. But that is simply not enough. This is hard with your own account (no rules and 100% dd allowed) let alone in a prop account (kind of designed with tight "risk controls", to use a really diplomatic term)

replies.author: Longjumping-Cook-842
replies.body:
Setting that as your goal with algo trading will probably lead to failure. Unless you already have a successful discretionary strategy that you are automating algo trading is going to be data driven and lives off of positive expectancy not r:r and wr.

Chances are you’re going to overfit every strategy you test just to fit those parameters.

replies.author: BarLeDuc9000
replies.body: Maybe try high rr with low win rate? Most of the prop trading have really tight dd requirements with consistency rules and trailing dd even. Which means that: what you would sanely use with your account ( a low rr high win rate), is not the best option for a prop account, given that such strategies often ladder up then get washed up ( dd spike) then they continue their slow ladder up (You have to figure the equity curve to get this example), this is really not what you want in a prop account.

comments.author: BarLeDuc9000
comments.body:
Maybe a bit of an edgy take but why don't you first try and trade manually. That will allow you to understand what you really need: 

You will see whatever behavior the market has that you cannot model, as in the prop feed may suck (I literally saw tradeify feed dying during Iran war peak) 

You can better understand why overlapping these indicators means nothing, you can better understand the importance of news and releases, and most importantly think in terms if continous time, fills, candlestick wicks and so on. 

Yes it will be slower but more productive than wasting time data mining hoping to randomly hit the jackpot (which is what you are doing now).

Afterwards use whatever "performance enhancement" you want to go turbo mode in your quant coding psychosis.

People may think manually trading is just ultra-slow inefficient overfitting. I'd argue it's a better use of you brain then chimping out on claude code for this specific instance
